notes:
Lead: CTO + Head of Product actively involved. Currently running production LLM features on another provider (OpenAI) -- exploring migration for cost predictability and regional residency. Key themes: compatibility, regressions, and operational predictability.

Summary of needs / ask:
- Start on Redwood Hosted to validate prompt parity and fail-safes, then migrate to Dedicated for steady-state throughput and lower unit economics.
- Need a compatibility shim/router so minimal engineering changes to call sites; want same REST/SDK semantics if possible.
- Must run comprehensive prompt parity tests (same prompts, compare tokenization + outputs). High sensitivity to subtle regressions in customer-facing chat flows.
- Latency target: median end-to-end <150ms for chat token generation in primary region (us-west). Throughput target: 30 qps sustained for embeddings + 200 concurrent chat sessions peak.
- Cost target: reduce per-embedding unit cost by ~30% versus current bills, and 20% reduction for chat tokens after Dedicated sizing.
- Security: SSO/SAML + audit logs + KMS integration. Data residency requirement: US-only for production corp data; PII redaction support preferred.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2026-01-15: Intro discovery call (AE Maya). Captured high-level workload and current spend.
- 2026-02-01: Demo of Redwood Hosted features (streaming, function call mocks) — Product team liked streaming but asked about tokenization parity.
- 2026-02-18: Fireflies call (ff_20260218_ValenceIntro) deep dive: engineering scoped migration effort (estimated 4–6 wks POC).
- 2026-02-27: Sent preliminary dedicated sizing + rough pricing (internal spreadsheet). Follow-up with pricing deck link.
- 2026-03-02: POC scoping meeting with SE (Diego) — agreed on three-phase POC: (1) smoke on Hosted, (2) compatibility shim + canonical prompt suite, (3) Dedicated sizing trial and canary. (ff_20260302_POC-scoping)
- 2026-03-05: Security questionnaire started; security doc shared (/drive/security/valence-security-qa.docx).
- 2026-03-09: Engineering team ran initial smoke test hitting Redwood Hosted endpoints; saw minor tokenization mismatch in system prompts. Logged as REDW-1347.

Customer quotes / color:
- CTO: "We can't ship a new chat experience if the model output drifts — regressions = support tickets and churn."
- Head of Product: "If Redwood can give us an easy compatibility layer and reliable latency, we're willing to commit to Dedicated."

POC plan (agreed):
- Phase 1 (1 week): Hosted API smoke — validate SDK calls, streaming and function-call hooks. Deliverable: smoke report + list of obvious prompt mismatches.
- Phase 2 (2–3 weeks): Compatibility shim that translates current provider's payloads/params to Redwood SDK, run canonical prompt suite (50 prompts across intents). Run A/B comparison and automated diff alerts for semantic drift.
- Phase 3 (2–3 weeks): Dedicated sizing trial (reserve GPUs), run throughput and latency SLO tests, and cost model comparison. Final decision based on parity pass rate (>95% intent parity), latency SLO, and projected ARR savings.

Engineering notes / asks for Redwood SE:
- Provide example compatibility shim repo or adapter pattern (Node + Python).
- Guidance on tokenization differences and tools to normalize prompts (tokenizer mapping, special tokens).
- Recommendations for batching/quantization profiles for Dedicated to meet cost targets.
- Canary rollout recipe: route 10% traffic to Redwood Hosted variant and measure error/regression metrics.

Next steps (short):
- SE Diego to run Hosted POC kickoff on 2026-03-12 (demo + shared repo).
- Send canonical prompt list (Valence to provide) and run first parity batch by 2026-03-19.
- Procurement to circulate contract baseline (pricing deck) internally this week.

Open questions / blockers:
- Will Redwood's tokenization/decoding change prompt engineering? How to ensure exact formatting for structured outputs.
- Data residency confirmation for Dedicated in us-west region + proof of KMS integration.
- Procurement threshold for committing to 12-month capacity (need finance ok).
